verdict.rationale: Meltano's own docs say it tracks incremental replication state, so later runs with the same state ID resume where the previous run stopped instead of reloading everything. That covers the state-management core of the story. The evidence does not say how cursors are chosen or whether changed (not just new) records are captured, and the claim comes only from vendor docs. missing for 10: documentation of cursor/replication-key handling, explicit coverage of changed-record (update/CDC) detection, independent or hands-on corroboration of incremental syncs.

support.subject: As a data engineer, syncs move only new and changed records — cursor and state management handled for me, not full reloads

citations.quote: keeps track of the incremental replication state, so that subsequent pipeline runs with the same state ID will always pick up right where the previous run left off
makes it easy to select which streams and properties to extract, and keeps track of the incremental replication state
